name: Notifications
plain: Asks to show alerts, banners and badges from the app.
meaning: Gives the app a direct line to the person's lock screen. Abuse is spam; legitimate uses are messages, delivery updates and security codes.

android.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't allow; apps targeting 33+ choose when to ask
android.persistence: Until revoked; existing apps are pre-granted on upgrade
android.store_policy: Play: no declaration, but data-safety disclosure for push
android.note: Apps targeting below 33 get the dialog automatically when they create their first channel.

ios.permission: none in Info.plist (runtime authorization); optional entitlements for time-sensitive and critical alerts
ios.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't Allow; provisional quiet delivery (iOS 12); Scheduled Summary (iOS 15)
ios.store_policy: App Review 4.5.4 push must not be required; no spam; critical alerts need Apple approval
ios.note: Provisional authorization delivers silently to Notification Center without a prompt.

data.update: per message; Android tracks per channel

limits.headline: Can show alerts, banners and badges, but only after you allow it
limits.user_action: You tap Allow when the app asks to send notifications
can: Show alerts, banners, sounds and badges once you allow
Ask at a good moment; apps for Android 13 or newer choose when
Deliver quietly to Notification Center on iPhone without a prompt, called provisional
cannot: Show alerts if you tap Don't allow or Don't Allow
Make you keep seeing them; you can turn them off any time in Settings
Show in Android 13 or newer without asking, unless it targets an older version
limits.differs: Both ask before the first alert. iPhone also has quiet provisional delivery. Android 13 and newer lets apps choose when to ask.

story.what_it_is: Asks to show alerts, banners and badges from the app.

marketing.name: Notification runtime permission
marketing.pitch: Android 13 added a runtime permission so people choose whether an app can send notifications.

story.for_you: You see a pop up asking Allow notifications. If you say yes, the app can ping you on your lock screen. You can change your mind in settings.
story.for_makers: Makers want this for chat, orders and security codes. Many also use it to bring you back, so asking at the right moment matters.

use_cases.example: A chat app asks right after you sign up so you never miss a message.
A food app asks to tell you when the driver arrives.
A bank app asks so it can send fraud and login codes.
A game asks after the tutorial so it can remind you when energy refills.
A social app asks to tell you about likes and follows.
A store asks to tell you about price drops.
A marketing team tests when to ask to get more yes answers.

story.android_note: Android 13 and up asks. Apps aimed at older versions get a pop up when they make their first channel.
story.ios_note: iOS offers a quiet delivery option and a scheduled summary.

technical_bounds: No prompt on iOS until the app asks
Android treats existing installs as granted
Android 13 needs two denials to be permanent; older upgrades keep the old grant
Foreground service notifications cannot be hidden
Per channel and Focus settings control delivery

linkedin.how: LinkedIn sends push notifications for messages, network activity and jobs; policy 2.3 lists push notifications as a communication channel. Members control categories in Settings.

history.change: Time Sensitive notifications and Notification Summary added
Provisional authorization and critical alerts introduced
Remote notifications with a user prompt on first registration
